# zlag2c

> Converts a complex double precision matrix to a complex single precision matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlag2c from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlag2c';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlag2c( order, M, N, A, LDA, SA, LDSA ) → integer
```

Converts a complex double precision matrix `A` to a complex single precision matrix `SA`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `SA` | `Complex64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix |
| ↳ `LDSA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `SA` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of lines of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N coefficient matrix A.
- `SA`: On exit, if `INFO=0`, the M-by-N coefficient matrix `SA`; if $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, the content of `SA` is unspecified.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `INFO` (0 = success, 1 = an entry of `A` exceeds single precision overflow)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to max(1,M) (column-major) or max(1,N) (row-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to max(1,M) (column-major) or max(1,N) (row-major)

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlag2c.strided(
    M, N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    SA, strideSA1, strideSA2, offsetSA
) → integer
```

Converts a complex double precision matrix `A` to a complex single precision matrix `SA`.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` (in complex elements) |
| `SA` | `Complex64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix (single precision simulated via Math.fround) |
| ↳ `strideSA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `SA` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideSA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `SA` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetSA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `SA` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of lines of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N coefficient matrix A.
- `SA`: On exit, if `INFO=0`, the M-by-N coefficient matrix `SA`; if $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, the content of `SA` is unspecified.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `INFO` (0 = success, 1 = an entry of `A` exceeds single precision overflow)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `= 1`: an entry of the matrix A is greater than the SINGLE PRECISION overflow threshold, in this case, the content of `SA` in exit is unspecified.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlag2c()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLAG2C`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlag2c.f).
-   Single precision quantization is simulated by applying `Math.fround` independently to the real and imaginary parts of each element; the output is still stored in a `Complex128Array`.
-   On overflow (`INFO = 1`), the contents of `SA` are unspecified, matching the Fortran reference behavior.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Complex64Array from '@stdlib/array/complex64/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret64 from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex64/lib/index.js';
import zlag2c from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlag2c';

const M = 3;
const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( M * N );
const SA = new Complex64Array( M * N );
const v = reinterpret( A, 0 );
let i;

for ( i = 0; i < 2 * M * N; i++ ) {
	v[ i ] = ( i + 1 ) * 0.5;
}
const info = zlag2c( 'column-major', M, N, A, M, SA, M );
console.log( 'info = %d', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( reinterpret64( SA, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLAG2C`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLAG2C converts a COMPLEX\*16 matrix, `SA`, to a COMPLEX matrix, A.

RMAX is the overflow for the SINGLE PRECISION arithmetic ZLAG2C checks that all the entries of A are between -RMAX and RMAX. If not the conversion is aborted and a flag is raised.

This is an auxiliary routine so there is no argument checking.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
